title: Application
summary: Vuetify comes equipped with a default markup that makes it easy to create layouts (boilerplate) for any Vue application.

title: Bottom sheets
summary: The bottom sheet component is used for elevating content above other elements in a dialog style fashion.

title: Buttons
summary: The button component communicates actions that a user can take and are typically placed in dialogs, forms, cards and toolbars.

title: Cards
summary: The v-card component is a versatile and enhanced sheet of paper that provides a simple interface for headings, text, images, and actions.

title: Chips
summary: The chip component allows a user to enter information, make selections, filter content or trigger actions.

title: Dialogs
summary: The dialog component informs a user about a specific task and may contain critical information or require the user to take a specific action.

title: Dividers
summary: The divider component is a thin line commonly used to separate groups of content in lists or layouts.

title: Expansion panels
summary: The expansion panel component is a lightweight container that hides information behind expandable and contractable containers.

title: Lists
summary: The list component is a continuous group of text, images and icons that may contain primary or supplemental actions.

title: Menus
summary: The menu component exposes a dropdown of potential selections or actions that the user can make.

title: Overlays
summary: The overlay component makes it easy to create a scrim over components or your entire application.

title: Sheets
summary: The sheet component is the baseline for many Material Design implementations used in Vuetify.

title: Toolbars
summary: The toolbar component sits above the content that it affects and provides an area for labeling and additional actions.

title: Tooltips
summary: The tooltip component displays textual information regarding the element it is attached to.

title: App bars
summary: The app bar component is a supercharged toolbar with advanced scrolling techniques and application layout support.

title: Bottom navigation
summary: The bottom navigation component is used for mobile devices and acts as the primary navigation for your application.

title: Breadcrumbs
summary: The breadcrumbs component is a navigational helper for pages. It can accept a Material Icons icon or characters as a divider.

title: Floating Action Buttons
summary: The floating action button (or FAB) component is a promoted action that is elevated above the UI or attached to an element such as a card.

title: Footers
summary: The footer component provides a container for displaying additional navigation information about a site.

title: Navigation drawers
summary: The navigation drawer component contains internal navigation links for an application and can be permanently on-screen or controlled programmatically.

title: Pagination
summary: The pagination component is used to separate long sets of data so that it is easier for a user to consume information.

title: Speed Dials
summary: The speed dial component is a floating action button that can reveal additional actions when clicked.

title: System bars
summary: The system bar component creates an android style status bar that rests on the very top of your application.

title: Tabs
summary: The tabs component provides a way to organize and navigate between groups of content that are related at the same level of hierarchy.

title: Autocompletes
summary: The autocomplete component provides type-ahead autocomplete functionality and provides a list of available options.

title: Checkboxes
summary: The checkbox component permits users to select between two values.

title: Combobox
summary: The combobox component provides type-ahead autocomplete functionality and allows users to provide a custom values beyond the provided list of options.

title: File inputs
summary: The file input component is a specialized input that provides a clean interface for selecting files, showing detailed selection information and upload progress.

title: Forms
summary: The form component provides a wrapper that makes it easy to process and control validation states of input components.

title: Inputs
summary: The input component is the baseline functionality for all of Vuetify's form components and provides a baseline for custom implementations.

title: Number inputs
summary: The number input component provides a clean interface for entering numeric values with increment and decrement controls.

title: OTP Input
summary: The OTP input component is used for MFA authentication via input field.

title: Radio buttons
summary: A radio button allows the user to choose only one of a set of options using a radio group.

title: Range Sliders
summary: The range slider component is a better visualization of the number input. It is used for gathering a range of numerical user data.

title: Selects
summary: The select component provides a list of options that a user can make selections from.

title: Sliders
summary: The slider component can be used as an alternative visualization instead of a number input.

title: Switches
summary: The switch component is a simple and eloquent toggle used to select between two values.

title: Text fields
summary: The text field component accepts textual input from users.

title: Textareas
summary: The textarea component is a text field that accepts lengthy textual input from users.

title: Calendars
summary: The calendar component is a clean and simple adaptation to the popular Google Calendar application.

title: Confirm edit
summary: The confirm edit component is used to allow the user to verify their changes before they are committed. This is useful when you want to prevent accidental changes or to allow the user to cancel their changes.

title: Data iterators
summary: The data iterator component is used for filter and displaying data including sorting, searching, pagination, and selection.

title: Data table - Introduction
summary: The data table component is used for displaying tabular data in a way that is easy for users to scan. It includes sorting, searching, pagination and selection.

title: Hotkeys
summary: The hotkey component displays keyboard shortcuts in a visually consistent and platform-aware manner.

title: Sparklines
summary: The sparkline component creates beautiful and expressive simple graphs for displaying numerical data.

title: Infinite scrollers
summary: The Infinite scroll component is a container that loads more items when scrolling. It is useful when you need to display an unknown but large number of items.

title: Tables
summary: The table component is a lightweight wrapper around the table element that provides a Material Design feel without all the baggage.

title: Treeview
summary: The treeview component is a user interface that is used to represent hierarchical data in a tree structure.

title: Virtual scrollers
summary: The Virtual scroll component is a container that renders only visible elements. It is useful when you need to display large amounts of uniform data.

title: Grid system
summary: Vuetify supports the 12 point Material Design grid for laying out and controlling breakpoints for your application.

title: Button toggles
summary: The button toggle component allows you to combine a series of selectable buttons together in a single element.

title: Carousels
summary: The carousel component is used to cycle through visual content such as images or slides of text.

title: Chip groups
summary: The chip group component combines numerous selectable chips into single or multiple lines.

title: Item groups
summary: The item group components provides the ability to create a group of selectable items out of any component.

title: Slide groups
summary: The slide group component is similar to item groups in that you can make selectable content out of elements but does so in a single line fashion.

title: Steppers
summary: The stepper component provides a linear progression process for gathering and displaying information to a user, similar to a form wizard.

title: Windows
summary: The window component is a wrapper container that allows transitioning between content. It serves as the baseline for tabs and carousels.

title: Alerts
summary: The v-alert component is used to convey information to the user. Designed to stand out, the alerts come in four contextual styles.

title: Badges
summary: The badge component is a small status descriptor for elements. This typically contains a small number or short set of characters.

title: Banners
summary: The banner component displays an important and concise message for a user to address. It can also indicate actions that the user can take.

title: Empty states
summary: The empty state component is used to indicate that a list is empty or that no search results were found.

title: Hover
summary: The hover component makes it easy respond when the user hover events by wrapping selectable content.

title: Progress circular
summary: The progress circular component is useful for displaying a visual indicator of numerical data in a circle.

title: Progress linear
summary: The progress-linear component is useful for displaying a visual indicator of numerical data in a straight line.

title: Ratings
summary: The star rating component is a specialized widget for collecting user feedback via ratings.

title: Skeleton loaders
summary: The skeleton loader component provides a placeholder loading state for when content is being fetched from a server or loaded asynchronously. It can be used in a variety of contexts, including cards, lists, and tables.

title: Snackbars
summary: The snackbar component informs user of a process that your application has performed is will perform. It can be temporary and often contains actions. Timer will stop when user hovers over the snackbar.

title: Timelines
summary: The timeline component is used to display chronological information either vertically or horizontally.

title: Aspect ratios
summary: The responsive component is used as a wrapper component to force custom aspect ratios for its children.

title: Avatars
summary: The avatar component is used to control the size and border radius of an image. It can be used with numerous components to provide better visual context.

title: Icons
summary: The icon component is compatible with multiple common icon fonts such as Material Design Icons, Font Awesome and more.

title: Images
summary: The image component provides a flexible interface for displaying different types of images.

title: Parallax
summary: The parallax component creates a 3d effect that makes an image appear to scroll slower than the window.

title: Color pickers
summary: The color picker component allows users to select a from pre-defined or custom colors using a variety of different inputs and formats.

title: Date pickers
summary: The date picker component is a stand-alone interface that allows the selection of a date, month and year.

title: Time pickers
summary: The time picker component is a stand-alone interface that allows the selection of hours and minutes in AM/PM and 24hr formats.

title: Defaults providers
summary: The defaults provider allows you to provide specific default prop values to components in a section of your application

title: Locale providers
summary: The locale provider allows you to modify the application's current language scoped within a template

title: Theme providers
summary: The theme provider allows you to style a section of your application in a different theme from the default

title: Lazy
summary: The lazy component allows you to dynamically render content based upon the user's viewport.

summary: The No SSR component is a simple component that doesn't get rendered on the server, but only on the client.

title: Mutation observer
summary: The mutation observer directive utilizes the Mutation observer API. It allows you to invoke a callback when targeted elements are updated.

title: Resize directive
summary: The resize directive provides the ability to conditionally invoke functions when the screen is resized.

title: Ripple directive
summary: The ripple directive adds touch and click feedback to any element in the form of a water ripple.

title: Scroll directive
summary: The scroll directive gives you the ability to conditionally invoke methods when the screen or an element are scrolled.

title: Tooltip directive
summary: The Tooltip directive is an easy to use implementation of VTooltip.

title: Touch directive
summary: The touch directive provides an interface for responding to various user touch actions.

title: Date inputs

title: File upload
summary: The file upload component is a drag and drop area for uploading files.

title: Icon Buttons
summary: The icon component is compatible with multiple common icon fonts such as Material Design Icons, Font Awesome and more.

title: Pie Chart

title: Progress
summary: A unified progress indicator component that supports both linear and circular variants with labels and accessible value formatting.

title: Pull To Refresh
summary: The PullToRefresh allows users to update content with a simple downward swipe on their screen.

title: Vertical Steppers
summary: The vertical stepper component is a navigation element that guides users through a sequence of steps.

title: Mask Inputs
summary: The mask input component is a input component for masking input values.

summary: The video component acts as a customizable wrapper for native video element.
